Concept:
SHM is described by a sinusoidal function of time, typically in the form y = A sin(ωt + ϕ), where
A is the amplitude, ω is the angular frequency, and ϕ is the phase constant.
Formula:
For SAM, the displacement function must be sinusoidal. Any function that can be written as y = A sin(ωt + ϕ) or y A cos(ωt + ϕ) represents SHM.
Calculation:
• (i) y = sin(ωt) – cos(ωt): This is a linear combination of sine and cosine, which can be written as a sinusoidal function, so it represents SHM.
• (ii) y = sin (ωt): This is not a sinusoidal function, as the cube of a sine function does not produce a simple sinusoidal motion, so it does not represent SHM.
• (iii) y = sin(ωt) + cos(2ωt): This is a sum of two functions with different angular frequencies, so it does not represent SHM because SHM requires a single frequency.
• (iv) y = 5 cos:
This is a sinusoidal function, so it represents SHM.
Answer: The correct answer is Option 3: Only (i) and (iv).
